literal: Earlier, Yuan Shun, acting Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, memorialized that the Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred offices and that official business ought not to be sent to the Censorate.
idiomatic: Before this, Yuan Shun, acting vice director of the Masters of Writing, argued that since that office is the root of government, routine business should not be routed to the censors.

literal: [5] When Zisi took office, he memorialized, saying:
idiomatic: [5] When Zisi came into the post, he submitted a memorial that said:

literal: I find in the Censorate statutes: "The Director supervises the hundred offices;
idiomatic: The Censorate regulations state: "The Director oversees the hundred offices;

literal: the Palace Clerk for Drafting impeaches and investigates within the forbidden precinct."
idiomatic: the drafting clerk investigates misconduct inside the palace."

literal: "It also states: "When the Director goes abroad, the hub of his carriage leads the way and the road is cleared for one li; kings, dukes, and the hundred ranks yield the road."
idiomatic: "They also say that when the Director travels abroad, his carriage hub goes before him, the road is cleared for a li, and kings, dukes, and all ranks step aside."

literal: That statute endured through four emperors; some twenty Directors in succession observed it in turn and it was never even briefly abandoned.
idiomatic: Four reigns had passed; some twenty directors in succession had lived by that rule, and it had never lapsed even briefly.

literal: The ministries, directorates, terraces, and secretariats all followed this statute.
idiomatic: Every ministry, directorate, terrace, and secretariat followed it.

literal: Only in Emperor Xiaozong's time, when mourning was held for Lintao, did the acting Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, my lord Shun, refuse to supply his name and also refuse to send the register.
idiomatic: Only under Emperor Xiaozong, during mourning for Lintao, had the acting left vice director Shun refused to list his name or send the attendance register.

literal: The former Director Li Daoyuan impeached and memorialized this, whereupon Shun again petitioned, saying, "The Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred offices; the Vice Directors are nobles who present counsel and ought not to be subordinated to the Director and have their names sent to the Censorate."
idiomatic: The former Director Li Daoyuan reported him; Shun answered with another petition: "The Masters of Writing are the root of government; vice directors who speak for the throne should not be made subordinates of the Director and have their names delivered to the Censorate."

literal: Shortly afterward he also received an edict approving his memorial.
idiomatic: Soon an edict approved his request.

literal: From then until now there has been no single standard.
idiomatic: Since then there had been no single standard.

literal: When I first entered the terrace I saw the affair in full and meant to petition for a binding decision, but because my post was concurrent I thought it premature to act at once.
idiomatic: When I first took my seat on the terrace I saw the whole affair and meant to petition for a firm ruling, but my post was only concurrent and I hesitated to move too soon.

literal: Day piled on day until hot and cold seasons had turned.
idiomatic: Days became months until seasons had turned.

literal: On the first day of last month the terrace sent notice to the Masters of Writing demanding the attendance roster for court, but the secretariat delayed and would not send it.
idiomatic: On the first of last month the terrace asked the Masters of Writing for the court attendance roster; the secretariat held it back.

literal: Soon another notice pressed them and named the chief clerk; suddenly a marginal note by Pei Xianbo, a gentleman of the Masters of Writing, read, "According to precedent, when the Director of the Censorate meets a terrace gentleman in the covered passage, the Director alights and holds his tablet while the gentleman on the carriage raises his hand in salute.
idiomatic: A second demand named the chief clerk; then Pei Xianbo, a gentleman of the Masters of Writing, added a marginal note: "By old precedent, when the Director meets a terrace gentleman in the covered passage, the Director dismounts with his tablet while the gentleman salutes from the carriage."

literal: From this it is clear they are not equals."
idiomatic: That shows they are not equals."

literal: When I saw this I was deeply astonished.
idiomatic: I was astonished when I read it.

literal: I turned the matter over two or three times and could not understand the reasoning.
idiomatic: I turned it over again and again and could not see the reasoning.

literal: I supposed the secretariat had separately received some new form and had altered Emperor Gaozu's old command, so I sent notice asking on what authority the matter rested.
idiomatic: I assumed the secretariat had received some new rule and set aside Emperor Gaozu's old order, and sent notice asking what authority they relied on.

literal: I also received a reply from Wang Yuanxu, another gentleman of the Masters of Writing, citing Cai Yong's Han Offices—it did not seem forced.
idiomatic: Wang Yuanxu, another gentleman of the Masters of Writing, answered with a passage from Cai Yong's Han Offices; it did not look far-fetched.

literal: Then I knew that Pei and Wang both meant to break the statutes; each wished to justify himself.
idiomatic: Then I understood that Pei and Wang meant to break the statutes—each trying to excuse himself.

literal: I find in the Han shu biography of Xuan Bing that an edict summoned Bing as Director of the Censorate; he and the Director of the Secretariat Police and the Director of the Masters of Writing met in the palace hall, each with a separate seat, and the capital called them the Three Who Sit Alone.
idiomatic: The Han shu biography of Xuan Bing records an edict summoning him as Director of the Censorate; he met in the hall with the Director of the Secretariat Police and the Director of the Masters of Writing, each with his own seat—the capital called them the Three Who Sit Alone.

literal: I also searched the Wei shu biography of Cui Yan and the Jin biography of Fu Gu of Wenyang [one graph deficient in the source]; both say that once he became Director, the hundred offices trembled in fear.
idiomatic: I also searched the Wei shu life of Cui Yan and the Jin life of Fu Gu of Wenyang, where one character is lost in the source; both say that once he was Director the hundred offices trembled.

literal: [6] From this it is clear that the Director has not bowed to secretariat gentlemen for a long time, and that the Censorate does not belong to the secretariat—this is not a matter of today alone.
idiomatic: [6] So the Director has not bowed to secretariat gentlemen in a long time, and the Censorate has never belonged to the secretariat—none of this began yesterday.

literal: I also find in the office statutes: "If one is late for court assembly, impeachment and censure follow at once."
idiomatic: The office statutes also say: "Late arrival at court is impeached on the spot."

literal: Then the registers of the hundred offices ought to be sent up to the terrace—this is plainly clear.
idiomatic: Registers of the hundred offices must therefore be sent to the terrace—plain as daylight.

literal: Again, violations of the statutes by the crown prince and below may all be investigated and censured; then the Vice Directors' names for court ought to be delivered to the Censorate—this too is obvious.
idiomatic: Anyone from the crown prince down who breaks the statutes may be investigated; vice directors' court names should go to the Censorate—equally obvious.

literal: If names are not delivered, by what proof are good and ill judged?
idiomatic: Without those names, how is merit or fault to be judged?

literal: Shun's stubborn insistence is not fair and even; that the former court indulged him—is that proper law?
idiomatic: Shun's stubbornness is not equitable; that the previous court indulged him was not proper law.

literal: I respectfully find that the gentlemen of the Masters of Writing Pei Xianbo, Wang Yuanxu, and others, though they stand among the elite and entered pure office early, lightly toyed with brief notes to this shining effect; clinging to heterodox views they suddenly reached this pass—if this is not disciplined, court commands will be ruined.
idiomatic: Pei Xianbo, Wang Yuanxu, and the rest stand among the elite and entered pure office early, yet they toyed with brief notes to this effect; clinging to perverse views they have come to this—if this goes unpunished, court orders will collapse.

literal: I ask that, on the evidence before us, Xianbo and the rest be removed from their posts and handed to the penal offices.
idiomatic: I ask that Xianbo and the others be removed from office on the evidence before us and handed to the penal offices.

literal: The Masters of Writing are the root of presenting counsel; the Vice Directors are the pivot of the hundred offices—like empty vanity they aid this perverse error; the ringleaders should be made plain and their crimes graded by degree.
idiomatic: The Masters of Writing are the root of counsel and the vice directors the pivot of government; aiding this error is empty vanity—the ringleaders should be named and punished by degree.

literal: The edict said, "States differ in government; one cannot rely on ancient affairs.
idiomatic: The edict answered: "States differ in government; ancient precedents cannot decide this.

literal: Hand the matter to the relevant office to examine Emperor Gaozu's old regulations, weigh gain and loss, and report."
idiomatic: Let the relevant office examine Emperor Gaozu's old regulations, weigh the rights and wrongs, and report."

literal: Shortly afterward Zisi's memorial was followed.
idiomatic: Shortly afterward the court followed Zisi's memorial.

literal: Still Yuan Tianmu resented it, and the matter was halted.
idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu, resentful, blocked it anyway.

literal: After Yuan Hao's defeat he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anding.
idiomatic: After Yuan Hao's defeat he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anding.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaojing he reached Attendant-in-Ordinary and died.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaojing he rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary and died.

literal: Chang's younger brother Zhen, courtesy name Golden Sparrow, inherited the title Baron of Ailing.
idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Zhen, courtesy name Golden Sparrow, inherited the barony of Ailing.

literal: [7] Under Emperor Shizong he curried favor with Gao Zhao and so won the emperor's intimate trust.
idiomatic: [7] Under Emperor Shizong he curried favor with Gao Zhao and won the emperor's intimate trust.

literal: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie died, Zhen led stalwart men to kill him.
idiomatic: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie died, Zhen led strong men to kill him.

literal: Later he died while Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He later died as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Ping's younger brother Changsheng held the posts of General of the Mobile Corps and Striking Cavalry.
idiomatic: Ping's younger brother Changsheng was General of the Mobile Corps and Striking Cavalry.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang, because his son Tianmu was powerful, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang, because his son Tianmu had grown powerful, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

literal: Tianmu's nature was mild and generous; he had a handsome face, was skilled at archery, and had a name for ability.
idiomatic: Tianmu was mild and open-handed, handsome, skilled with the bow, and known for ability.

literal: At twenty he first left home to serve as supernumerary gentleman.
idiomatic: At twenty he entered service as a supernumerary gentleman.

literal: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, Li Chong, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Guangyang Shen marched north to punish them; Tianmu was sent on mission to comfort the armies.
idiomatic: During the Six Garrisons rebellion, Li Chong, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Guangyang Shen marched north; Tianmu was sent to comfort the troops.

literal: Passing through Xiurong, Erzhu Rong saw that his orders were orderly and that he had the air of a commander; they formed a deep bond and swore brotherhood.
idiomatic: Passing Xiurong, Erzhu Rong saw his commands in good order and a commander's bearing; they bonded deeply and swore brotherhood.

literal: Before long Rong asked that Tianmu be made mobile-office commissioner; the court did not agree and instead appointed him separate commander, ordering him to proceed to Xiurong.
idiomatic: Soon Rong asked that Tianmu be made mobile-office commissioner; the court refused and made him a separate commander bound for Xiurong.

literal: At that time the northern garrisons were in turmoil and uprisings flared everywhere; the Six Garrisons were swept away with no border defense left—only Rong stood on the main road, gathering the scattered and the lost.
idiomatic: The north was in chaos; the Six Garrisons were gone and the border undefended—only Rong, on the main road, gathered wanderers.

literal: Tianmu was Rong's confidant and was made Regional Inspector of Bingzhou.
idiomatic: Tianmu was Rong's confidant and was made regional inspector of Bingzhou.

literal: When Rong went to Luoyang, Tianmu took part in the first plot; Rong then left Tianmu behind as rear guard to support him.
idiomatic: When Rong marched on Luoyang Tianmu helped plot the move; Rong left him behind as rear guard.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Tianmu, through Rong's favor, was specially made Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang, and summoned to the capital.
idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's accession, through Rong's favor, Tianmu was made Grand Commandant and Prince of Shangdang and summoned to court.

literal: When Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, an edict made Tianmu front-army commander-in-chief, leading the capital host to join him.
idiomatic: When Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, an edict made Tianmu commander of the van with the capital armies.

literal: When Rong captured Ge Rong, Tianmu's fief was increased to thirty thousand households in all with his prior grants.
idiomatic: After Rong captured Ge Rong, Tianmu's fief rose to thirty thousand households in all, counting earlier grants.

literal: Soon he supervised the national history, recorded Masters of Writing affairs, opened a government office, and hereditarily held Bingzhou.
idiomatic: Soon he supervised the national history, recorded Masters of Writing affairs, opened a government office, and held Bingzhou in perpetuity.

literal: Earlier Du Luozhou and Xianyu Xiuli had raided; many in Ying and Ji provinces fled south to escape the disorder.
idiomatic: Earlier Du Luozhou and Xianyu Xiuli had raided, and many in Ying and Ji fled south.

literal: Xing Gao of Hejian, former chief clerk of the former Northern Ping prefecture, [8] led his followers and held Moying city against Luozhou and Ge Rong for nearly three years.
idiomatic: Xing Gao of Hejian, [8] former chief clerk of Northern Ping, led his band and held Moying against Luozhou and Ge Rong for nearly three years.

literal: After Prince of Guangyang Shen and the others were defeated, Gao crossed south and settled on the border of Beihai in Qingzhou.
idiomatic: After Shen, Prince of Guangyang, was defeated, Gao went south and settled on the Beihai border in Qingzhou.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered that wherever refugees gathered, commandery and county jurisdiction should be assigned and local magnates chosen as administrators to pacify them.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered refugees registered to commanderies and counties, with local magnates as administrators to pacify them.

literal: Then Regional Inspector of Qingzhou Yuan Shijun memorialized to establish Xin'an commandery with Gao as administrator; no reply came.
idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Qingzhou Yuan Shijun asked to create Xin'an commandery and make Gao administrator; no reply came.

literal: When the terrace reviewed appointments to commanderies and counties, [9] because Gao's nephew Ziyao ranked higher by inherited privilege, the post of Administrator of Hejian was given instead.
idiomatic: When the terrace reviewed county appointments, [9] Gao's nephew Ziyao ranked higher by inherited privilege and received Hejian instead.

literal: Gao was deeply shamed and angry, and thereupon rebelled.
idiomatic: Gao was shamed to the bone and rebelled.

literal: Refugees who had long been bullied by locals heard Gao had risen and flocked to him; within a month and a half his host passed a hundred thousand.
idiomatic: Refugees long bullied by locals heard and joined him; within a month his force passed a hundred thousand.

literal: They plundered hamlets and harmed the people; the people of Qi called them the "Bald-elm bandits."
idiomatic: They looted villages and harmed civilians; Qi people called them the Bald-elm Bandits.

literal: Earlier men of Henan had often mocked men of Hebei for eating elm leaves, and so the name was taken from that.
idiomatic: Henan men had mocked Hebei men for eating elm leaves—hence the nickname.

literal: Gao raided east into Guang province, reaching the sea before returning.
idiomatic: Gao raided east into Guang province to the sea and back.

literal: He also defeated the army of Area Commander Li Shuren.
idiomatic: He also broke the army of Area Commander Li Shuren.

literal: An edict ordered Tianmu and the Prince of Qi, King of Qi Xianwu, to campaign and smash them utterly.
idiomatic: An edict sent Tianmu and the King of Qi Xianwu to crush them.

literal: Gao then asked to surrender; he was sent to the capital and executed.
idiomatic: Gao surrendered, was sent to the capital, and beheaded.

literal: Tianmu's fief was increased by ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Tianmu's fief grew by ten thousand households.

literal: At that time Yuan Hao seized Yingyang while the emperor was exposed; hearing that Emperor Xiaozhuang was touring the north, Tianmu crossed north from Bigong Rampart and met the imperial carriage at Henei.
idiomatic: Yuan Hao seized Yingyang; hearing the emperor had gone north, Tianmu crossed from Bigong Rampart and met him at Henei.

literal: Erzhu Rong, because the season was fiercely hot, wished to withdraw the army; Tianmu pressed hard that he must not, and Rong yielded.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, finding the heat fierce, wished to withdraw; Tianmu insisted and Rong yielded.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Tianmu was made Grand Preceptor with feather canopy and martial pipes;
idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang returned to the palace Tianmu was made Grand Preceptor with feather canopy and martial pipes;

literal: his fief was increased to seventy thousand households in all with prior grants.
idiomatic: his fief rose to seventy thousand households in all.

literal: Tianmu was a distant kinsman without real virtue or standing; relying on the Erzhu clan his rank reached the utmost; at the time he blazed so bright that court and country trembled; from kings and dukes down the gate was full every morning as they brought gifts—treasures piled up.
idiomatic: A distant kinsman without standing, he rode the Erzhu to the summit of rank; court and country trembled; kings and dukes packed his gate each dawn with gifts until treasures piled high.

literal: Yet he was broad and gentle toward others and was not much hated in his day.
idiomatic: Yet he was broad and easy with people and not much hated.

literal: The emperor, because he was Rong's faction, outwardly showed him favor and ordered that Tianmu might enter and leave by the Great Sima Gate in carriage or on horseback.
idiomatic: Xiaozhuang, because he was Rong's man, showed outward favor and let him pass the Great Sima Gate by carriage or horse.

literal: Tianmu and Rong leaned on each other; their trust was especially deep.
idiomatic: He and Rong leaned on each other with uncommon trust.

literal: Rong always treated him with the rites due an elder brother, while Erzhu Shilong and the rest, though Rong's sons and nephews and already of heavy rank, feared Tianmu and bowed low to please him.
idiomatic: Rong treated him as an elder brother; Shilong and the other Erzhu nephews, though already grandees, feared Tianmu and bowed to please him.

literal: When Tianmu once spoke of Shilong's fault, Rong at once had him beaten—their intimacy went that far.
idiomatic: Once Tianmu named Shilong's fault and Rong had Shilong beaten at once—such was their bond.

literal: The emperor inwardly feared and hated him; he was killed together with Rong.
idiomatic: The emperor feared and hated him inwardly; he was killed with Rong.

literal: At the start of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously made Chancellor, Pillar General of the State, and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou, with the yellow battle-axe lent, posthumous title Martial-Splendid.
idiomatic: At the Deposed Emperor's accession he was posthumously made Chancellor, pillar general, and regional inspector of Yongzhou, with the yellow battle-axe lent, posthumous name Martial-Splendid.

literal: His son Yi inherited; he had fine talent and looks.
idiomatic: His son Yi inherited—talented and handsome.

literal: He held the post of Director of the Ministry of Justice.
idiomatic: He was Director of the Ministry of Justice.

literal: When Qi received the mandate he heard the summons, feigned illness, and died of fright.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate he heard the summons, feigned illness, and died of fear.

literal: Duke of Xihe Dun was a great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.
idiomatic: Duke of Xihe Dun was a great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.

literal: At the start of Emperor Taizu's campaigns he followed on campaign, bore hard armor and sharp blades, and his name stood first among the generals.
idiomatic: At the start of Taizu's wars he followed on campaign in hard mail with a sharp edge, first among the generals.

literal: Later he followed the campaign against Zhongshan; wherever he turned none could stand before him.
idiomatic: Later, campaigning against Zhongshan, none could stand before him.

literal: Under Emperor Taizong he was made Grand Palace Steward of the Center.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he was made Grand Palace Steward of the Center.

literal: Under Emperor Shizu his rank advanced to Duke of Xihe and favor grew still deeper.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu he was advanced to Duke of Xihe and favored still more.

literal: He died; his son Bo inherited.
idiomatic: He died; his son Bo inherited.

literal: Minister of Works Shi was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.
idiomatic: Minister of Works Shi was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.

literal: Loyal and brave with stratagem, he was especially skilled at mounted archery.
idiomatic: Loyal, brave, and resourceful, especially skilled at mounted archery.

literal: He followed Emperor Shizu on the southern campaign as far as Guabu.
idiomatic: He followed Shizu south as far as Guabu.

literal: He held Director of the Masters of Writing and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.
idiomatic: He was Director of the Masters of Writing and regional inspector of Yongzhou.

literal: He passed through Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Regional Inspector of Hua, [10] and was promoted in succession to General Who Conquers the South.
idiomatic: He served as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and regional inspector of Hua, [10] and rose to General Who Conquers the South.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Duke of Works.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Duke of Works.

literal: General of the Martial Guard Wei was the fourth son of Emperor Lie.
idiomatic: General of the Martial Guard Wei was the fourth son of Emperor Lie.
